Stacked on #684 (lyric machine). Adds 12 PRIM3 study tapes to `data/albums.json` (album `prim3`), with lyrics from the #684 machine, all `reviewed:false`.

**Order:** Got WiFi? stays first. The other tracks follow the PRIM3 course order in `mcclusterishere/Prim3` → `learning/course/course-feed.json`, S01E01 to S07E03. `data/` has no course list of its own. In the course, Got WiFi is S02E03. It stays first as instructed.

## Tracks

| # | Title | File | Lyrics source | Lines | Flagged | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Got WiFi? (existing) | got-wifi.mp3 | unchanged | | | |
| 2 | High Alert | high-alert.m4a | auto | 60 | 3 | 0.806 |
| 3 | OSINT | osint.mp3 | aligned | 35 | 9 | 0.859 |
| 4 | Anti-Social Engineering (Draft) | anti-social-engineering.mp3 | aligned | 60 | 24 | 0.543 |
| 5 | Red, Blue, Purple, White Team | red-blue-purple-white-team.mp3 | auto | 35 | 2 | 0.83 |
| 6 | Data Breach | data-breach.mp3 | imported (DistroKid TTML) | 59 | 0 | n/a |
| 7 | App Attacks | app-attacks.mp3 | aligned | 31 | 5 | 0.744 |
| 8 | Dive In | dive-in.mp3 | **none: the upload is the instrumental** | | | |
| 9 | IOT (Draft) | iot.mp3 | aligned | 8 | 0 | 0.73 |
| 10 | Per Diem (Draft) | per-diem.mp3 | aligned | 27 | 5 | 0.776 |
| 11 | RAID (Hot Site) | raid-hot-site.mp3 | aligned | 63 | 9 | 0.701 |
| 12 | Evil Twin (Middle Man) | evil-twin-middle-man.mp3 | aligned | 80 | 17 | 0.694 |
| 13 | Ghost in the Wires | ghost-in-the-wires.mp3 | aligned | 58 | 12 | 0.733 |

**Audio:**
- Embedded metadata and cover art are stripped. The codec is kept.
- High Alert is AAC in an M4A container despite its `.mp3` name (checked with ffprobe), so it ships as `.m4a`.
- Red/Blue/Purple/White Team was supplied as a 32-bit float WAV. It ships as a 320 kbps MP3 web copy. The repo keeps no masters, so the WAV is not committed.

**Engine:** Demucs htdemucs_6s, then faster-whisper **small.en**, then wav2vec2 CTC. This used small.en instead of the default because the container had under 1.2 GB of free disk. Auto lines for High Alert and Red/Blue/Purple/White Team are rougher than a large-v3-turbo run would be. Re-run with `--force` on Core or CI before review if wanted.

## Drafts
`albums.json` has no draft flag, so these tracks have `(Draft)` in the title:
- Per Diem
- Anti-Social Engineering
- IOT

Their audio files use the final slugs (`per-diem.mp3` and so on), so a final can replace the file in place. Their catalog keys include `-draft` (`prim3:per-diem-draft`), so the key changes when the title loses "(Draft)".

Anti-Social Engineering has 24 of 60 lines flagged: the draft take departs from the sheet. The IOT sheet has only 8 lines for a 72-second take.

## RAID check
`raid-hot-site.mp3` has the same byte size and duration as Evil Twin, but a different MD5. Bigram overlap between the recogniser's transcript and each sheet:

| Recording | Its own sheet | The other sheet |
|---|---|---|
| RAID | **0.45** | 0.04 (Evil Twin) |
| Evil Twin | **0.47** | 0.02 (RAID) |

RAID is a separate song that matches its own sheet, so it is added.

## Dive In
- Its vocal stem averages -61 dB, which is silence.
- Whisper on the full mix hears only hallucinations.

So the upload is the instrumental. It is on the shelf with no lyrics, and its sheet is at `data/lyrics/src/dive-in.txt`, waiting for the vocal take. The format test exempts it explicitly.

Note: after merge to `main`, the lyric-machine workflow (`--missing`) would try Dive In against that sheet. The output is an artifact only and should be discarded.

## Sheets waiting for audio
Kept as reference and not wired to tracks:
- `data/lyrics/src/white-grey-black-hat.txt`
- `data/lyrics/src/cap-ex-vs-op-ex.txt`
- `data/lyrics/src/patch-work.txt`
- `data/lyrics/src/iaas-saas-paas.txt`

## Derived
- `seconds` in `albums.json` and `workers/mccluster/src/music/tracks.js`
- `data/catalogue.json` and `catalogue.html` (13 tracks on the shelf)
- `llms.txt` now says 41 registered tracks
- Pending seed `supabase/pending/20261031190000_prim3_catalog_objects.sql` and its rollback. Not applied.
- The sitemap check passes with no change.
- The Equity Uprise verifiers pass with no source-map change.

Tracks without an ISRC take house numbers in shelf order, so the Whip Equipped tracks move from QT6KV·19–27 to QT6KV·31–39. These numbers are not ISRCs.

## Tests
- `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`: 1300 pass, 0 fail.
- Core `lyrics-machine.test.mjs`: 18 pass, 0 fail.
- Worker `music-gate` and `prim3-curriculum-map` tests: 30 pass, 0 fail.
- Lyrics e2e (Playwright 1.58.2, `serviceWorkers:'block'`): 328/328 checks, with 30 tracks played including the 11 new timed PRIM3 tracks.
- Control lyrics review e2e: 23/23.
- New test: PRIM3 order, files present, no ID3 tag or covr atom, lyrics `reviewed:false`, reference sheets kept and not on the shelf.

## Needs the owner
- **ISRCs** for the 12 tracks. None are minted, so none are in the MusicRecording graph yet.
- **Credits:** producers and features. The tracks currently carry the album default "Music to build to.".
- **Dive In vocal take.**
- **Finals** for the three drafts.
- **Review** of all lyrics in Control → Create → Music → Lyrics, especially the two auto tracks and Anti-Social Engineering.

Owner: "I don't like the way control room is designed right now. I think it needs a major consolidation of services." Then, after the mockup: "get that control room under wraps".

This PR builds the approved consolidation mockup into the real Control Room (`control.html` + `js/control-room-v2.js` + `js/control-room/*`). It changes the UI only: no backend, table, Worker or migration changes. It is merged up to date with main at e80cb0a, which includes #678 direct sales and #680 deploy gates.

## One navigation definition
`js/control-room/nav.js` (`window.CR.nav.NAV`) defines six sections → items (the tabs) → optional views (a segmented control inside an item). Every entry has `id`, `label`, `route`, `renderer` and `was`. `was` lists the old routes and old names that now live in that entry. NAV drives:
- the one `<nav id="crSections">`. On a phone it is the bar: Home, People, Sell, Create, and More, which opens Insights and System. From 1024px it is the sidebar. Next to the shared site bar it becomes a row under the topbar, so the page still has only one bottom bar.
- the ⌘K palette. Its entries come from NAV leaves and are searchable by old names ("desk bot", "crm", "vault"…).
- `js/control-registry.js`, which feeds the owner palette on other pages.
- `js/control-room/workspace-core.js` routes. These feed the shared bar's Control destination panel, whose groups are now Home/People/Sell/Create/Insights/System/Products, and the `?workspace=1` owner preview.

These other navigation lists are removed: the hand-written rail and `.cr-bottom` in control.html, `SURFACES`, the typed `WORK_VIEWS`/`CREATE_VIEWS`/`SYSTEM_VIEWS` lists (now derived from NAV), the old palette list, and the registry's own list.

## IA: old view → new home
| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `#home` | Home → Today (`#home:today`): AI command bar, numbers, Needs you, Working now, System pulse, Recent activity, Public record |
| `#ai` | Home → Ask McCluster (`#home:ask`), with the full durable chat and voice |
| `#work:inbox` | People → Inbox → Conversations (each conversation has an **AI reply** switch, which is the thread mode) |
| `#work:desk-bot` | People → Inbox → AI reply (KB, spend, refusals, channels, tools) |
| `#work:people` | People → Contacts |
| `#work:companies` | People → Companies |
| `#work:pipeline`, `#work:tasks` | People → Deals → Pipeline / Next actions |
| `#work:clients`, `relationships`, `projects`, `deliverables` | People → Clients → Clients / Relationships / Client projects / Deliverables |
| `#work:outreach` | People → Outreach |
| (new) | Sell → Orders → All orders: one list with type chips |
| `#work:orders`, `#work:bookings` | Sell → Orders → Order records / Bookings |
| `#work:payments`, `#work:renewals` | Sell → Payments & renewals |
| `#work:operations` | Sell → Store → Shop & operations |
| #678 / (mount) | Sell → Store → Direct sales (#678's `CR.musicDirect`, live) / Marketplace (`CR.marketplace`, #679, not available yet) |
| `#create:music` | Sell → Music → Review & catalog (its own Direct sales tab from #678 stays) |
| (mount) | Sell → Music → Lyrics & stems (`CR.lyrics`) |
| `#create:projects`, `#create:library` | Create → Projects & library |
| `#create:channels`, `instagram`, `schedule` | Create → Publish → Channels / Instagram / Schedule |
| `#create:front-page`, `clipping`, `song-test` | Create → Front page / Clipping / Song test |
| `#analytics` | Insights → Overview. Each Insights item is an analytics-deck chapter (Audience, Journeys, Content, Action & business, World intelligence, Cameras, Adaptive, Site health, Data explorer), and the deck is unchanged |
| (new entry) | Insights → Halo globe, a door to `action-globe.html?explore=1&halo=1` (One Halo) |
| `#system:overview`, `command`, `workload`, `observability`, `resources` | System → same names |
| `#apps` | System → Apps |
| `#create:build` | System → Build |
| `#create:action-network`, `#create:funding` | System → Equity Uprise ops → Missions & fellows / Funding |

**Needs you** collects:
- owner approvals (`core.resume` pending approvals, Approve/Deny via `/v1/ai/approvals/:id/decision`);
- open orders from every order source;
- unanswered threads;
- marketplace seller applications, once `CR.marketplace.applications()` exists;
- lapsed renewals and failed payments, read from the Work records' `state`;
- the existing attention items.

**Sell → Orders** reads print-shop and merch-shop leads, booking leads, `/v1/work/orders` and `/v1/work/bookings` records (by `state`), the owner's `music_orders` (RLS-scoped, refetched on Refresh, failures not cached), and `CR.marketplace.orders()` when that module exists. Each row opens where its order lives. The tables are not merged.

## Mount points
A NAV view whose `module` is registered on `window.CR` renders and binds that module. Otherwise it renders "not available yet".
- Sell → Store → Direct sales is live: it shows #678's `window.CR.musicDirect`.
- `#sell:store:marketplace` waits for `window.CR.marketplace` (#679).
- `#sell:music:lyrics` waits for `window.CR.lyrics` (the lyrics PR).

Those PRs only need to register `{render(), bind?()}`.

## Compatibility
- Every old hash resolves through `CR.nav.resolve()` and is replaced (not stacked) with its new route. That covers `#work:*`, `#create:*`, `#system:*`, `#ai`, `#analytics`, `#apps`, `#home`, and the old `normalize*View` aliases (`#work:crm`, `#create:vault`, `#system:logs`…).
- The ten compat pages are now minimal redirect stubs: admin, crm, desk, studio, management, lanes, vault, music-admin, inbox and insights. Their URLs still work and point at the new routes.
- `js/tabbar.js` lights Analytics for `#insights:*`. The shared bar's links (`#home`, `#analytics`) still land.

## Deleted
- Dead bodies of the 10 compat pages (about 2,400 lines)
- `js/office.js`: only the removed bodies loaded it
- `js/socials-room.js`: only management.html loaded it
- `css/ops-polish.css`: only crm, desk and management used it
- `scripts/test/polish-wave-two.test.mjs`: it tested the deleted stylesheet
- the dead `.cr-rail` / `.cr-nav__item` / `.cr-bottom` rules in `css/control-room.css`, and the `.cr-bottom` rules in `css/control-analytics.css`

## Kept on purpose (checked with git grep)
- `js/mc-analytics.js`: the Worker's site-analytics loader serves it
- `css/control-connections.css`: used by `js/control-room/connections.js`
- `js/control-palette.js`: the owner palette on console, catalogue, ecosystem, analytics, mnet, album and listen
- `js/music-admin.js`: the creator-release review client. Security tests (expected version, hash-pinned listen) still assert it.
- `css/control-room.css` (v1): it is not merged into v2, because console.html, analytics.html, account.html, catalogue.html and ecosystem.html still load it. Only its dead rules were removed.

## Design
The look follows the mockup, using the existing `--cr-*` tokens, dark Control and the ruby accent. Layout is mobile-first (hard rule 14): new rules use `min-width` queries only, `minmax(0,1fr)`, inputs at `max(16px,…)`, and `scrollWidth===clientWidth` is checked at 390/820/1280. The only mark is the supplied `assets/img/hm-mark-wide.webp`, scaled whole. `docs/control-plane/SHARED-NAVIGATION.md` records the one-NAV contract. On control.html the shared bar keeps the bottom of the screen, so the Control sections are a row under the topbar on a phone and the sidebar from 1024px.

## Tests (at the merged head)
- `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`: **1329 pass / 0 fail**
- New `scripts/test/control-nav.test.mjs`:
  - every old view id and bare surface (37) is claimed by exactly one leaf;
  - old aliases and compat targets land;
  - every renderer exists and mount points are declared;
  - the palette finds views by old names;
  - every navigation surface reads NAV.
- New `scripts/e2e/control-room-nav.e2e.mjs` at 390/820/1280: **187/187**. It checks that:
  - all six sections render;
  - the bar, sidebar, More sheet and palette come from NAV;
  - 16 old routes redirect, and a cold load of an old route is replaced;
  - mount points behave: Direct sales renders the registered module, Marketplace and Lyrics show "not available yet";
  - Work rows are read by `state`: Problems/Done counts and labels, and exactly one lapsed renewal and one failed payment in Needs you;
  - Refresh refetches music orders after a failed read, and after a changed order;
  - there is no horizontal overflow and no console error.
- Existing suites:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| control-desk-bot | 78/78 |
| control-front-page | 90/90 |
| control-build-code | 42/42 |
| funding-register | 16/16 |
| site-navigation | 243/243 |
| control-workspace | 64/64 |
| analytics-tabs | 356/356 |
| analytics-unified | 164/164 |
| analytics-measurement | 65/65 |
| connections | 19/19 |
| news-context | 32/32 |
| site-health | 76/76 |

  The analytics, connections, news-context and site-health suites were run before the merge.
- `analytics-globe.e2e` was not run locally: it needs the Cesium CDN and a global Playwright browser the sandbox does not have. It runs in Control workspace visual proof.
- Equity Uprise verifiers: all six pass. `equity-uprise-repo-source-map-v2.json` adds `js/control-room/nav.js` and drops the deleted or stubbed sources. It was regenerated after the merge, and the generated report is normalized to `/home/runner/work/mccluster/mccluster`.
- Old-layout assertions were updated to the new routes: `#crViewSelect`, `#work:*` hashes, `.cr-rail`/`.cr-bottom` and the Studio filter. No security or a11y assertion was weakened.
- `control-workspace-visual.yml` now also runs `control-nav.test.mjs` and `control-room-nav.e2e.mjs`. No Worker code was touched.

## Follow-ups
- **Backend CRM unification.** People → Contacts/Companies/Deals/Clients/Outreach is a UI consolidation over three CRM backends (`leads` + `/v1/work/*`, `out_*`, `crm_contacts`/`crm_touches`). The tables stay as they are; unifying them is a separate, reviewed migration.
- **Creator-release review.** `music-admin.html` has redirected into Control for a while, so `js/music-admin.js` (operator release review with hash-pinned listening) has no reachable UI. It should become a Sell → Music view.
- **Marketplace and lyrics.** #679 registers `CR.marketplace` (`render`, optionally `orders()` and `applications()`). The lyrics PR registers `CR.lyrics`.
- **Phone bar on control.html.** Should the Control section bar replace the shared bar on control.html? That is an owner call; today the shared bar keeps the bottom.

**Stacked on #684.** Merge #684 first. GitHub then retargets this PR to `main`.

## What and why
The owner asked (2026-10-31): "anything that's uploaded, it should strip it, like every audio from each instrument, like be able to track out the whole instrumentation plus the vocals."

The lyric machine in #684 already separates every track. This PR keeps all of the stems, stores them privately, and lets the owner work with them in Control.

### Separation
- **Model:** Demucs `htdemucs_6s` gives vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano and other. `htdemucs` (four stems) is the fallback. Every run also writes an **instrumental** mix (everything except the vocals). The manifest records the model used.
- **Format: 320 kbps MP3.** Measured across 11 tracks, all seven files for one track come to 18–46 MB. FLAC would be lossless but roughly twice that or more, and these stems are for listening, practice, remix sketches and handing to an engineer. `STEMS_FORMAT=flac` re-runs a single track losslessly.
- **No clipping.** The measured separations peaked as high as **+3 dBFS**, so they clipped when encoded. The separator now applies **one shared gain** to every file, which keeps the stems' balance (they still add up to the mix), and records it as `gain_db`. Re-separated Towyard Killer and Repo Guy now peak at -1.0 and -2.1 dBFS after encoding. The manifest schema refuses anything above 0 dBFS, which is how this was caught.

### Private storage (nothing in the public repo)
- **Audio:** the existing private bucket `mcc-gated-audio`, under `stems/<track_key>/<stem>.mp3`. No bucket or storage-policy change: the bucket is already private, and only the service role signs URLs for it.
- **Manifest:** `public.music_stem_sets`, in `supabase/pending/20261031190000_music_stem_sets_v1.sql` (with rollback). It records the model, format, stems, sizes, SHA-256 hashes, and peak and RMS levels. RLS is on, and anon/authenticated access is revoked: service role only.
- **Keys:** a shelf track uses its slug; an upload uses `ct-<creator track uuid>`.
- The CLI keeps stems in `~/.cache/mccluster/stems/<slug>`, never inside the published checkout.

### McCluster Core
- **New executor, `stems_separate`.** Shelf audio is fetched only from `https://matthew.mccluster.org/assets/audio/…`; an upload's master is downloaded with the service key. It separates, uploads, and writes the manifest. It is also exposed as the `stems.separate` capability (`owned`/`compute`, no paid API).
- **`lyrics_align` now keeps the stems** its own separation already made for an upload. A stems failure never fails the lyrics.

### Owner access
- **`music-access` actions:** `operator-stems-list` signs a play URL and a download URL for each stem, valid 15 minutes. `operator-stems-queue` asks Core to separate, or separate again. Both are `houseOps` only, and only `stems/<key>/<stem>.<ext>` paths are ever signed.
- **Control → Create → Music → Stems** (`js/control-room/stems-panel.js`), phone first:
  - every stem plays together on one Web Audio clock, with a transport and a seek bar;
  - **Solo** and **Mute** on each instrument, and "Play alone" on the instrumental;
  - **Save** (download) for every file;
  - **Separate stems** / **Re-run separation**.

### CLI
`node tools/lyrics/stems.mjs <audio> [--out DIR] [--model htdemucs_6s|htdemucs] [--format mp3|flac] [--upload]`

## Measured on this container (4 vCPU)
Demucs `htdemucs_6s` over the 11 tracks the lyric machine ran on. Times are separation only. These files were not uploaded anywhere.

| Track | Length | Separate (s) | 7 files |
|---|---|---|---|
| Test Drive | 1:35 | 33.5 | 26.7 MB |
| Salvage Title (B-Side) | 1:29 | 36.7 | 25.0 MB |
| Repo Guy (B-Side) | 2:00 | 45.4 (52.9 re-run with gain) | 33.7 MB |
| Hundun (B-Side) | 2:23 | 56.5 | 40.1 MB |
| Towyard Killer | 1:06 | 25.3 (31.6 re-run with gain) | 18.4 MB |
| Mr. Lock Changer (Remix) | 1:48 | 50.8 | 30.3 MB |
| Lana (B-Side) | 1:25 | 31.1 | 23.9 MB |
| Stand On Business (B-Side) | 2:01 | 42.0 | 33.8 MB |
| All in the Details | 2:35 | 68.4 | 43.4 MB |
| Who Did The Shoot | 2:10 | 62.2 | 36.4 MB |
| Environmental Injustice | 2:43 | 62.3 | 45.6 MB |

Separation runs at about 0.4× real time on CPU. The whole shelf is roughly 0.4–0.5 GB of stems.

## What needs owner action
1. Deploy Core with #684 and this PR, using the lyric runtime from #684 (Demucs is already part of it).
2. Apply `supabase/pending/20261031190000_music_stem_sets_v1.sql`.
3. Deploy `music-access`.
4. Separate the shelf: in Control use **Separate stems** per track, or run `node tools/lyrics/stems.mjs … --upload` with service credentials.

**Commercial option, not implemented:** AudioShake, if a paid separation quality tier is ever wanted.

## Tests
- `core`: 377 pass. New `stems.test.mjs` covers the manifest schema, private upsert uploads under `stems/`, key validation, the executor's shelf-URL restriction, upload keys, and that `lyrics_align` keeps stems while a stems failure never sinks the lyrics.
- `scripts/test`: 1302 pass. New `stems-private.test.mjs` checks that the operator gate is the first thing the stems actions do, that only stem paths are signed, that the table has no anon/authenticated grants, and that stems never default into the checkout. `live-callers.json` lists the pending-only table.
- `deno check music-access`: clean.
- e2e `scripts/e2e/control-stems.e2e.mjs`: **18/18** at 390 px and desktop. All seven files load, play on one clock, solo/mute/"play alone" set the mix correctly, pause stops every source, there is a download per stem, a track with no stems queues Core with its key and audio, every target is at least 44 px, there is no sideways scroll, and a non-operator sees the refusal and never fetches stem audio.
- e2e `control-lyrics-review` from #684: still 23/23.

prs.body:
## What and why

The owner asked (2026-10-31) for the missing Whip Equipped songs to go into the repository as tracks, and for a lyric timestamping machine that works out the lyrics automatically whenever something is uploaded. He then added lyric sheets, the film/album treatment, and this request: "put it together with every single song that has lyrics."

### 1. Nine tracks, in story order
`data/albums.json` → `whip-equipped` now has 11 tracks, ordered by the owner's treatment: Test Drive, Salvage Title (B-Side), Repo Guy (B-Side), Hundun (B-Side), Dealer Plates (A-Side), Dealer Plates (B-Side), Towyard Killer, Mr. Lock Changer (Remix), Lana (B-Side), Stand On Business (B-Side), All in the Details. **The owner can reorder them in `data/albums.json`.**

- **Audio:** copied into `assets/audio/<kebab-slug>` with `ffmpeg -map_metadata -1 -c copy`, so the codec is unchanged and the titles and cover art are stripped. **Towyard Killer** was named `.mp3` but is actually AAC in an M4A container, so it ships as `.m4a`. The repo's audio goes from 67 MB to 100 MB; the largest file is 6.2 MB. No LFS is needed, and this is far under the Pages limit.
- **Track data:** `seconds` comes from `scripts/music-track-lengths.mjs`, which also regenerates `workers/mccluster/src/music/tracks.js`. Poster: `assets/img/wing-whip-poster.jpg`. Each track has an optional short `story` blurb taken from the treatment; existing readers ignore it.
- **No `credit`:** the repo's convention for tracks without a known producer is to leave the field out.
- **Regenerated files:** `data/catalogue.json` (29 tracks), `catalogue.html`, `llms.txt` (29 registered tracks), and a pending catalog-objects seed (below).
- **The music graph now lists only ISRC-registered recordings.** The new tracks have no ISRC yet, because the ledger is append-only and minted by the owner. They are on the shelf and in the registry list, and join the graph once minted.
- **Entity rules:** this is Matthew's music on matthew.mccluster.org. The album shares its name with Whip Equipped LLC, Matthew's separate company, and the story doc says so.

### 2. The story, made canon
The repo had no earlier storyline, so the treatment becomes canon at `docs/music/WHIP-EQUIPPED-STORY.md`.
- It has a header (canon, owner 2026-10-31, fiction, entity note) and a track table in story order.
- The owner's text is kept as written. Each broken `Attachments/…` link is replaced by the repo track it refers to, or by "not yet in the repo".

### 3. The lyric machine (`core/src/lyrics/`)
Five stages, each replaceable. The JSON records which model ran each stage and how long it took.

1. **Separator:** Demucs `htdemucs_6s`, which returns every stem (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other), an instrumental mix, a manifest, and a 16 kHz vocal (`separate.py`). `htdemucs` is the 4-stem fallback.
2. **Recogniser:** faster-whisper on the isolated vocal (`asr_faster_whisper.py`).
   - A second pass re-listens to long stretches with no words, which recovers sung intros Whisper skipped.
   - Known hallucinations ("Thanks for watching") are filtered out.
   - Passing the sheet as `initial_prompt` is optional and off by default: on Hundun it made Whisper collapse the intro into one segment.
3. **Mapper:** the owner's sheet (`align.mjs`) is mapped to the recognised words.
   - Global word alignment keeps the owner's lines, line breaks and sections.
   - It is repeat-aware: a hook or intro the sheet writes once but the song sings again is placed again with the owner's words (`repeat: true`).
   - Where the audio clearly differs, what's sung wins and the line is flagged (`mismatch`, `heard`, `sheet`, `added`).
   - With no sheet, the recognised words are broken into lines.
4. **Aligner:** wav2vec2 CTC forced alignment, WhisperX-style, of each line's words against the vocal (`ctc_align.py`, torchaudio `WAV2VEC2_ASR_BASE_960H`).
5. **Tidy + validate:** times stay inside the song, never go backwards, and words stay inside their lines.

**Accepted inputs:**
- Plain text, `.docx`: a bounded ZIP reader for `word/document.xml`; DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations are refused and nothing is executed.
- DistroKid **TTML** and **LRC**: line times are kept from the file; word times come from the audio when it is available, otherwise they are spread evenly. These files get `source: "imported"`.

**Output** is the existing `data/lyrics` shape, `timed.line[] {begin, end, content}` in seconds, plus optional fields that older readers ignore: `words[] {begin, end, content}`, `section`, `confidence`, `align_score`, `mismatch`, `heard`, `repeat`, `added`, a top-level `source` (`aligned` / `auto` / `imported` / `owner`), `reviewed: false`, and `machine {engine:{separator, asr, aligner}, timing, …}`. Owner sheets are kept as text in `data/lyrics/src/<slug>.txt`.

### Where it runs, and why
- **Choice:** McCluster Core (OVH, `core/`), as a `lyrics_align` executor on the existing `ops_agent_jobs` queue, exposed as the `lyrics.align` capability (`owned` / `compute`).
- **Why not Workers AI:** the self-host-first policy ranks owned/compute above metered. Whisper alone can't separate vocals or force-align, and Demucs plus wav2vec2 need a persistent CPU process with ffmpeg, which is what Core is. There is no new backend, no new queue, and no paid API, so there is no spend to approve.
- **Commercial alternative (not implemented):** AudioShake for separation/alignment, if a paid quality fallback is ever wanted.
- **Same engine everywhere:**
  - Offline CLI: `node tools/lyrics/transcribe.mjs <audio> --out data/lyrics/<slug>.json [--sheet …|--timed …]`, or `--missing --wire`.
  - CI: `.github/workflows/lyrics-machine.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch` and on push to main touching audio, albums or sheets. It uses `contents: read`, **never pushes**, and uploads the generated JSON plus `albums.json` as an artifact for review (hard rule 2).

### How the auto-trigger on upload works
1. On `creator.html`, the release form takes an optional lyric sheet: pasted, or a `.docx` / `.txt` / `.lrc` / `.ttml` file read in the browser by `js/lyric-sheet.js`. It is attached after the release row is written, and a refusal never sinks the upload.
2. `supabase/pending/20261031180000_lyrics_machine_v1.sql` (with rollback) adds `creator_tracks.lyrics_sheet` and a trigger. When a release gets a master, or its master or sheet changes, the trigger queues **one** `lyrics_align` job for the house org.
3. Core downloads the master with its service key, runs the pipeline, and writes `creator_tracks.lyrics` unreviewed. The player already renders that inline.
4. **Lyrics the owner reviewed are never overwritten**: the PATCH itself filters on `reviewed`.

### Owner review: Control → Create → Music → Lyrics
`js/control-room/lyrics-review.js`, built for phone width first.
- Pick a track. It plays, and the playing line lights up.
- Flagged lines are marked with what McCluster heard, and a **Flagged** filter shows only those.
- Fix the words. Tap a time to hear the line; −/+ nudges it 0.1 s; **Now** stamps the line to the playhead.
- Tick **These lyrics are right** to mark them reviewed.
- Saving depends on where the lyrics live:
  - **Shelf tracks** live in the repo, so the corrected `<slug>.json` downloads, to commit or hand to Build. There is no new write backend.
  - **Uploads** use new owner-only actions on the existing `music-access` function (the `houseOps` check): `operator-lyrics-get`, `operator-lyrics-save` and `operator-lyrics-queue` (re-run on Core).

### Synced lyrics in every player
`js/lyrics-sync.js` is one shared renderer. It reads every shape on the shelf (`timed.line`, the older `lines[]`, plain text).
- **album.html** now uses it: the current line lights up and scrolls into view, words light as they're sung where word times exist, tapping a line seeks to it, and nothing shifts while it plays (color/opacity only). The deck-bar one-liner uses it too.
- **music-videos.html** uses the same reader.
- **The World** keeps its tested self-contained `lyricLines`, which already accepts both shapes.

**Inventory of the shelf's lyric files:**
- 19 tracks have lyrics; all are timed now.
- `who-did-the-shoot.json` and `environmental-injustice.json` were **text only**. They are now aligned from their own text, which is kept in `data/lyrics/src/`.
- The two unwired variant files (`environmental-injustice-brave.json`, `money-or-the-power.json`) are untouched: the shelf uses their `.dk.json` versions.

## What needs owner action
1. **Deploy Core** with this commit, and install the lyric runtime on the VPS: ffmpeg plus a venv with `torch/torchaudio 2.7.1 (cpu)`, `faster-whisper 1.2.1`, `demucs 4.1.0`. Set `LYRICS_PYTHON` in `/etc/mccluster/core.env` (steps in `core/README.md` → "Lyric machine runtime"). The first run downloads the weights: about 1.6 GB for large-v3-turbo, 80 MB for Demucs, 360 MB for wav2vec2.
2. **Then apply** `supabase/pending/20261031180000_lyrics_machine_v1.sql`. Applied before Core is deployed, Core quarantines the jobs as unsupported.
3. **Apply** `supabase/pending/20261031180100_whip_equipped_catalog_objects.sql` to make the 9 tracks live discovery objects.
4. **Deploy the `music-access` function** for the Control save and re-run actions.
5. **Mint ISRCs** for the 9 tracks (QT6KV ledger) when ready; they then join the music graph.
6. **Review lyrics** in Control → Create → Music → Lyrics. Everything machine-made here is `reviewed: false`.
7. **Credits:** all 9 new tracks have no producer credit. Tell us if they should say "Prod. …".

## Quality per track
All runs used separation → recognition on the vocal → CTC alignment. Recognition used **medium.en**: large-v3-turbo did not fit this container's disk quota. Production defaults to large-v3-turbo. Times are per stage on 4 CPU cores.

Release notes

Sourced from supabase/setup-cli's releases.

v3.0.1

Summary

  • Allow the CLI's own registry fallback instead of pinning every recent CLI to GHCR (#453). The GHCR default is kept for CLI versions before v2.108.0; newer versions are free to fall back, which reduces exposure to GHCR image-pull throttling.
  • An explicit registry choice by the caller is still preserved.
  • Dependency bumps for ruby/setup-ruby and dev tooling.

Validation

  • CI and E2E passed on main before tagging.

v3 is the moving major-version alias for this release.

v3.0.0

Summary

  • Install the Supabase CLI from the npm package instead of GitHub releases.
  • Support latest, beta, and fixed npm package versions.
  • Remove the github-token input; npm is now the source of truth for CLI resolution and install.
  • Preserve caller npm configuration by running npm from the workspace while keeping the action-owned install isolated.
  • Improve musl/Alpine runtime handling for existing node and npm binaries.

Validation

  • CI and E2E passed on main before tagging.
  • All open pull requests were cleared before release.

v3 is the moving major-version alias for this release.

v2.1.2

Allow Supabase CLI v2.108.0 and newer to use its built-in image registry fallback by default. Older CLI versions retain the GHCR default, and explicit registry selections remain unchanged.

v2.1.1

Fix Alpine/Linux musl containers that do not already include the C++ runtime libraries required by Bun and the Supabase CLI shim.

prs.body:
Owner, 2026-10-30: "I want my stripe integration to please treat this as a marketplace so others can also sell their merch on it. Remember, its productization we're aiming at here."

**Nothing here touches production.** The SQL is pending (not applied), nothing is deployed, and nothing was written to Stripe. Do not merge before the rollout below is approved.

## Owner decisions this implements
- **The seller is the seller of record.** Each seller gets a Stripe Express account. Each sale is a DIRECT charge on that seller's account, and McCluster takes its cut as `application_fee_amount`: the same model as `workers/mccluster/src/connect.js`, whip and l3. A checkout is for one seller only; there is no mixed-seller cart.
- **The platform cut is 15% and only the server sets it.**
  - The database constant `public.marketplace_platform_fee_bps()` = 1500 and the code constant `MARKETPLACE_PLATFORM_FEE_BPS` (in `workers/mccluster/src/merch/fee.js`) must be equal; two tests check this.
  - The fee is charged on item subtotal plus shipping, never on sales tax: fee = round((subtotal + shipping) × 1500 / 10000). Sellers cannot change it.
- **Anyone can apply.** An applicant finishes Stripe-hosted Express onboarding. The owner approves each seller in Control before any of its listings is public, and can suspend a seller or remove a listing.
- **Fulfilment in v1: the seller ships, US only.** Paid orders appear in the seller's dashboard. The seller marks each order packed, shipped (carrier and tracking required) or delivered, and the buyer follows it on a status page.
- **Stripe Tax fails closed. There is no config flag, on purpose.**
  - `automatic_tax` is always on, and prices and shipping are tax-exclusive.
  - Before any stock is held, checkout reads the seller's `GET /v1/tax/settings` (with `Stripe-Account`). If the status is anything but `active`, checkout answers 409 `seller_tax_not_ready`.
  - If Stripe rejects a session for a tax reason, checkout fails the same way and releases the unit.
  - Why no flag: a flag that turns tax off is a switch for selling untaxed, with the seller (the merchant of record) carrying the liability.
  - **Sellers set up tax themselves inside Stripe's embedded Connect components on the Sell page.** Details under "Sales tax" below.
- **Print on demand (Printful) is the next PR. v1 leaves the slot for it:**
  - listings and variants carry `fulfilment_mode` (`seller_ships` | `pod`, default `seller_ships`) and nullable `pod_*` fields;
  - orders carry nullable `provider_order_id` / `provider_status`;
  - `marketplace_seller_providers` holds only a `credential_ref`, never a token; RLS is forced and browsers are closed out;
  - a database CHECK publishes only `seller_ships` in v1. No Printful API calls are made.

## Architecture: where things live and why
- **Seller, listing, checkout, order and admin API: `/v1/merch/*` on Worker `mccluster`** (`workers/mccluster/src/merch/router.js`).
  - It sits next to the canonical Connect rail it reuses: `connect.js` creates the Express account and builds account links, and `org_stripe_accounts` holds its state.
  - It also reuses `whip/stripe.js` for Stripe requests, Supabase Auth, and the house `ops.use` grant via `requireCapability`.
  - No new backend, auth, billing, CRM or admin.
- **Proof of payment: the canonical `stripe-webhook` Edge Function.** Marketplace settlement lives in `marketplace.ts`; endpoint secrets in `endpoints.ts`.
- **Data: Supabase `zmnhbrjyhxzhkxmhkexs`**, in the pending file `supabase/pending/merch_marketplace_v1.sql`. A seller is an org (`orgs`, `org_members`, `org_stripe_accounts`).
- **Pages: McCluster Corp's marketplace under `market/`.**
  - Hosted on matthew.mccluster.org so sessions and checkout returns work, as `DOMAINS-AND-ENTITIES.md` prescribes for company apps. Listed as company pages, branded McCluster Corp, and `noindex` until go-live.
  - Only the supplied M mark is used, unaltered.
- **Control: Work → Marketplace** (`js/control-room/marketplace.js`) to approve and suspend sellers, remove listings, and see platform-fee totals.

## Money flow
1. The buyer picks a listing, an option and a quantity. The browser sends nothing else.
2. The Worker checks that the seller's tax setup is `active`.
3. `marketplace_order_create()` checks visibility and stock, takes the unit, prices the order from database rows, and computes the fee. Only the SHA-256 of a random buyer token is stored.
4. The Worker re-checks the fee against its own constant. If they disagree it refuses and releases the unit.
5. Stripe Checkout opens on the seller's account with:
   - `application_fee_amount` set to the database fee;
   - `automatic_tax`, a fixed shipping rate, US addresses only;
   - metadata `kind`, `marketplace_order_id`, `mccluster_org_id`, copied to the PaymentIntent as well.
6. The webhook settles the order (see Security). The seller ships and adds tracking. The buyer follows the status by token.
7. Refunds happen on the seller's account with `refund_application_fee: true`. The refunded amount on the order only grows, and a refund does not restock.
8. When a checkout expires, its unit goes back.

**Stock rules**
- **Reserved at checkout.** Taking the unit when payment arrives would let two buyers pay for the last one.
- **Never written from a snapshot.** This fixes Codex P1 (review comment 4425597626).
  - After a listing is created, a variant's stock changes only inside the order functions or `marketplace_variant_set_stock()`, a compare-and-set against the count the seller loaded (`expected_inventory`; a mismatch answers 409 `stock_changed` and the page reloads).
  - The variant guard refuses any other stock write, for every role, including the service role.
- **Waiting listings go live when the second of these arrives:** seller approval or Stripe readiness. This fixes Codex P2 (review comment 4425597633).
  - `marketplace_release_waiting_listings()` does it, called by approval and by a trigger on `org_stripe_accounts`.
  - Sellers can move a `pending_review` listing back to draft.

## Sales tax (go-live path)
Express accounts have no Stripe Dashboard page for tax, so the Sell page embeds Stripe's own Connect components.

- **What the seller sees:** a "Sales tax" step in the dashboard.
- **What the seller sets up there:**
  - `tax-settings`: head office and preset product tax code;
  - `tax-registrations`: the states where the seller collects;
  - Stripe's `notification-banner`.
- **How the page loads them:** Connect.js comes from Stripe's CDN (`https://connect-js.stripe.com/v1.0/connect.js`), and the page calls `StripeConnect.init` with the publishable key and `fetchClientSecret`.
- **How the session is minted:** by `POST /v1/merch/seller/account-session`.
  - It only ever opens the caller's **own** seller account. No org or account is read from the request.
  - It is refused to shop staff and to sellers McCluster has not approved, and refused before Stripe has the seller's details.
  - It enables only `tax_settings`, `tax_registrations` and `notification_banner`.
  - It needs `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` in the same mode as `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`.
- **Until tax is active**, checkout keeps failing closed.
- **CSP:** none applies. The pages are static GitHub Pages without a CSP; the Worker sets CSP only on hosts it serves itself.

## Security binding
- **Webhook binding to the order.** `marketplacePaymentRefusal()` binds the event to:
  - the order row;
  - the connected account stored on the order, which must equal `event.account`;
  - the stored checkout session id;
  - livemode and the seller org;
  - currency;
  - the server's subtotal and shipping, with no discount, and total = basis + Stripe tax;
  - the session being paid.

  `marketplace_order_mark_paid()` checks the same again under a row lock. An order is paid only from pending under its stored session; a replay changes nothing. Only a bound sale is booked in the commerce ledger, in the seller's org.
- **Connected-accounts endpoint.**
  - `stripe-webhook` now also accepts `STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (and `STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TEST`), tried after the platform secrets.
  - An event the platform secret verifies behaves exactly as before, including events with `event.account`.
  - An event only a Connect secret verifies must name a connected account. Otherwise it gets a 400, so a platform-only event signed by the Connect secret is refused.
  - A Connect-verified event never reaches a platform-only effect (premium plan, music licence grant/expiry/failure/refund). It may settle a marketplace order, sync `org_stripe_accounts` and the providers flag on `account.updated`, and write the org-scoped commerce ledger.
  - A test secret accepts only test-mode events.
  - Documented in `SECURITY-POSTURE.md` and `docs/stripe-webhook.md`.
- **Guards for every role.**
  - Order terms are immutable and payment facts are written once.
  - Order status transitions are whitelisted, and orders are never deleted.
  - Stock gate as above.
  - A listing is published only for an approved seller with a ready Stripe account, and only `seller_ships`.
  - Images must be objects the server recorded for that seller (`marketplace_assets`). Ownership comes from the record, not the path (the #666 lesson).
- **RLS.**
  - The public reads only visible listings and approved sellers' public columns.
  - Seller members read their own drafts and orders.
  - Buyers read through `marketplace_order_by_token()`, which shows city and state only.
  - Money and moderation functions are `service_role` only, with `search_path=''` pinned.

## Rollout (each step needs the owner's approval)
1. **SQL.** Review and apply `supabase/pending/merch_marketplace_v1.sql`. Promote it as `supabase/pending/README.md` → "To promote one" describes, take a production snapshot, and drop its names from `live-callers.json`. It needs only what production has. Until it is applied, `/v1/merch` answers 503.
2. **Stripe dashboard (test mode first, then live):**
   - Connect settings: Express enabled; McCluster Corp branding (icon, colour); US `card_payments` + `transfers` capabilities. Fix the platform business profile and statement descriptor first: it still says "Street Credit Bureau" (activation gate 3 in `docs/action-network-financial-architecture-decision.md`).
   - Connected-accounts webhook: add an endpoint for `https://zmnhbrjyhxzhkxmhkexs.supabase.co/functions/v1/stripe-webhook` with "Listen to events on Connected accounts", subscribed to:
     - `checkout.session.completed`
     - `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`
     - `checkout.session.expired`
     - `charge.refunded`
     - `account.updated`

     Set its signing secret as **`STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`** on the `stripe-webhook` function, and the test-mode endpoint's as `STRIPE_CONNECT_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TEST`.

     Check which endpoint the existing `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` belongs to: `docs/stripe-webhook.md` says it was once created with "connected accounts" ticked. If it was, it keeps working unchanged (the platform secret is tried first).
   - Embedded components: confirm Connect embedded components are available on the platform. Set **`STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`** (`pk_test_…` / `pk_live_…`, matching the mode of `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`) on Worker `mccluster`.
3. **Deploy.** Deploy Worker `mccluster`, then the `stripe-webhook` function, from `main` after merge. The Worker's `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and the function's `STRIPE_SK` must be the same platform account and mode.
4. **Test mode end to end.** In order: apply, onboard, approve in Control, Sell → Sales tax (head office + one registration) until tax shows active, list, buy with 4242, ship, refund. Check:
   - the order is paid with tax;
   - the seller org's `work_orders` row exists;
   - Control shows the fee;
   - stock moves only with orders;
   - a listing published before Stripe is ready goes live when onboarding finishes.
5. **Go-live.** Remove `noindex` from `market/*`. After the first real sale, add a door on the company page (`data/seo/company-site.json`, which has its own evidence rules).

## Test results (local, worktree, commit `5389eef8`)
- `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`: 1302/1302 pass.
  - Includes `merch-marketplace.test.mjs`, 10 tests: every signing-secret/event combination (including a platform-only event signed by the Connect secret being refused), binding negatives, ledger mapping, fee parity, stock gate, release trigger, the POD check, the Connect.js origin, and mobile-first CSS.
  - The reconciler contract tests were updated to the endpoint policy.
- `cd workers/mccluster && npm test`: 1260/1261. The new merch tests pass 11/11:
  - an Account Session only for the caller's own approved account, with only the tax components;
  - refused for staff, unapproved shops, not-onboarded accounts, a missing key and a mismatched key mode;
  - stale stock refused with 409, and no PATCH carries stock;
  - back to draft.

  The one failure, `observability-instrumentation` ("fal gateway client is not installed"), also fails on `main` here because there is no `node_modules`. Unrelated.
- `bash scripts/test-merch-marketplace-db.sh` on scratch Postgres 16: pass. Adds the stock-gate scenarios (a direct write is refused for every role; a stale compare-and-set is refused; a title edit during a reservation keeps the count; expiry still restocks) and both event orders for waiting listings.
- `deno check supabase/functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts`: pass.
- Playwright 1.58.2 (`scripts/e2e/merch-marketplace.e2e.mjs`), mocked network: 126/126 at 390, 820 and 1280.
  - Every page reached `scrollWidth === clientWidth`, and controls are at least 16px.
  - Adds the Sales tax step: a Connect.js fixture mounts the banner, tax settings and tax registrations, and the page asks for its session with no account in the request. Also covers back-to-draft and `expected_inventory` on edit.
- Equity Uprise verifiers (repo sources, program coverage, authority hygiene): pass.

## Follow-ups (out of v1 scope)
1. **Printful print on demand.** Each seller links their own Printful account via your referral link; orders are submitted automatically; shipping and tracking come back through webhooks. The slots are already in the schema.
2. Book McCluster's application fee as house revenue from `application_fee.created` / `application_fee.refunded`, pro rata on partial refunds. Today the fee lives on the order and in `control_audit`.
3. A scheduled sweep that releases pending orders past `expires_at` if an expiry event is never delivered. Add a per-IP checkout rate limit, because a 35-minute stock hold can be abused.
4. A buyer order email carrying the status link.
5. Multi-seller cart, international shipping, music-creator Connect payouts (`creator_profiles.payout_state`), retiring the legacy `pay-now` / `connect-onboard`, and seller subscriptions.

Analytics currently overstates what browser events establish: preview endings can inflate an unpaired completion ratio, volume and weighted actions have misleading labels, later device logins inherit anonymous history, and playback duration includes paused wall time. This draft repairs those behaviors in the existing pipeline.

Changes:
- Audience Science v3 keeps preview/full reports separate, returns unavailable for unpaired completion rates, and assigns accounts only through the same raw/lean event ID.
- Page performance exposes exact legacy formulas and unknown denominators. Signup Journeys v3 excludes anonymous/other-account history and client-stored attribution claims; all identity reads are first-party scoped.
- First-party transport allowlists diagnostic/click/copy payloads, strips URL secrets and recognizable sensitive values, and flushes late hidden/pagehide producers with keepalive. Genuine errors and the exact injected-browser signature remain.
- Static/Creator discovery and World share browser-progress measurement: fresh attempt IDs, ordered sequences, valid progress seconds, and explicit gaps/discontinuities. Starts follow actual playing; rejected requests remain errors; preview endings are separate. Existing event IDs remain stable on retries. Observed withdrawal or cross-tab consent removal permanently invalidates cumulative playback counters; later measurement starts a fresh attempt.
- Two dormant, unused SQL proposals partition Visitor evidence by event identity and prevent tenant deletion from nulling retained event scope. They are tested only in isolated PostgreSQL/WASM. No production schema changes.

Validation:

## Summary
Owner, 2026-10-15: "People should be able to sign up to Whip Equipped real quick. When they try to use it, it'll just tell them the service is not done, but if you know a driver, or you are a driver, have them sign up today." The voter rule is gone (PR #440). Whip Equipped LLC is Matthew's separate company. Everything here uses its own name and none of McCluster's branding.

## What changed and why
- **`workers/mccluster/src/whip/launch-gate.js`**: a McCluster-side wrapper that runs in front of the lifted Whip handlers in `src/index.js`. The lifted files are untouched (README: they stay byte-identical).
  - `GET /api/service-status` returns `{rides_live:false, operator:"Whip Equipped LLC", message, driver_signup_url, driver_consent_version, driver_consent_text}`.
  - `POST /api/rides`, `POST /api/rides/:id/payment-intent` and `POST /api/rides/:id/accept` return **HTTP 503** `{code:"service_not_live", error/message:"Whip Equipped rides aren't live yet. Are you a driver, or know one? Have them sign up today.", operator, driver_signup_url:"https://matthew.mccluster.org/whip/driver/"}`. Nothing is dispatched and no database call is made. Rides go live only when the owner sets the Worker var `WHIP_RIDES_LIVE=true`.
  - `POST /api/drivers/me` is the driver application:
    - The applicant must be signed in.
    - Only fields the existing 0037 `drivers` table holds are accepted: name, plate, optional phone, make/model/colour, seats.
    - It needs `application_consent:true` plus the current `consent_version`.
    - The row is saved `online:false` and unverified (the same as the lifted handler).
    - The response is `approved:false`, with the message "Applying is not approval: Whip Equipped's own checks (identity, driver licence, insurance, background check and local rideshare rules) decide who drives."
    - Fields that imply approval (`online`, `identity_verified`, `approved`, `status`, `rating`, `tenant_id`, `auth_user_id`) are refused.
    - An applicant who already has a row gets `already_received` and no second row is created.
- **`supabase/pending/whip_driver_application_consent_v1.sql`** plus a rollback: two nullable columns on Whip's own `public.drivers`, `application_consent_at` and `application_consent_version`. A CHECK requires both or neither, and RLS is unchanged.
  - **This is not applied.** Until it is, sign-up answers `503 driver_signup_not_ready` rather than save an application without its consent.
- **Whip apps in this repo:**
  - The Driver app (`whip/driver/`) shows "Apply to drive" with the consent checkbox and text, says rides aren't live yet, and shows the server's not-approval message. Phone width first, inputs at 16px, `minmax(0,1fr)`.
  - The Rider app (`whip/rider/`) shows a "Rides aren't live yet" sheet with the driver sign-up link when the API answers `service_not_live`.
- Quick sign-up for riders uses the existing account flow (`/api/auth/signup`, the M Account). No rider waitlist table existed, and none was added.

Production check (SELECT only, 2026-10-15): the 0037 tables exist (`tenants`, `drivers`, `rides`, `identity_verifications`, `partner_catalog`, `partner_referrals`, `sales_leads`, `operator_members`). There is 1 driver, 0 rides and 0 identity verifications. `drivers` has no consent column.

## Tests run
- `cd workers/mccluster && npm ci && npm test`: **653 pass, 0 fail**. This includes `test/whip-launch-gate.test.mjs` (9 tests):
  - `service_not_live` through the real `entry.js` for all three ride routes, signed in and out, with CORS and no database call
  - `WHIP_RIDES_LIVE`
  - pass-through of the other routes
  - driver validation (consent required, approval fields refused, bounds)
  - a signed-out 401, a 400 with fields, `already_received`, and the insert shape
  - 503 when the consent columns are missing
  - the lifted files untouched
- `node --test scripts/test/*.test.mjs`: **628 pass, 0 fail**.
- `scripts/test-whip-driver-consent-db.sh` on a scratch Postgres 16 (0037, the pending file twice, behaviour, rollback, re-apply): **ok**.
- `python3 docs/design/equity-uprise-building/production/verify_equity_uprise_repo_sources.py`: `"passed": true`.
- Driver app rendered in Playwright at 390 and 1280: `scrollWidth === clientWidth`, inputs 16px, the consent text is shown, and the submit posts `application_consent:true` with the current version.

## Risk notes
- `POST /api/drivers/me` no longer reaches the lifted `gateway.js` create. The wrapper does the same insert plus consent. Until the migration is applied, the production Driver app's "create driver profile" answers 503 `driver_signup_not_ready`. It used to create a row with no consent.
- Ride routes are closed while `WHIP_RIDES_LIVE` is unset. Production had 0 rides.

## Rollback
Revert this PR and redeploy the Worker. If the migration was applied, export the consents, deploy the previous Worker, then run `whip_driver_application_consent_v1.rollback.sql`.

1. Apply `supabase/pending/whip_driver_application_consent_v1.sql` (Supabase MCP `apply_migration`), then promote it per `supabase/pending/README.md`.
2. Deploy the Worker.

prs.body:
## Why

`checkout` and `music-checkout` take money, but nothing recorded it anywhere McCluster could see. The Stripe webhook settled music entitlements and nothing else. In production every `work_*` table is empty and `stripe_events` has never held a row. `work_payments.verification = 'provider_verified'` existed, but nothing could set it.

## What changes

After the signature is verified, `stripe-webhook` calls service-role database functions:

| Stripe event | Effect |
|---|---|
| `checkout.session.completed` (paid) / `async_payment_succeeded` | buyer becomes a lead (found by email, or created as `confirmed`) → `paid` order (`source_table = stripe_checkout`) → `provider_verified` payment → the follow-up the sale implies: a monthly or annual renewal, a proposed booking plus a "Schedule…" task for deposits, "Ship … to …" with the address, "Deliver … to …", or "Follow up: …" |
| `charge.refunded` | full refund: payment `refunded`, order `cancelled`; partial refund: noted on the payment; an unknown payment answers `matched:false` and nothing is invented |
| `invoice.paid` (after the first) | renewal payment linked to the renewal and its order; dates advance |
| `customer.subscription.deleted` | renewal `cancelled` |

- **Exactly once.** Unique indexes on order source and payment provider reference, one renewal per subscription and one booking per order, plus a per-session advisory lock. A repeat delivery returns the same ids. A failed write answers 500 so Stripe retries.
- **Tenancy.** A connected-account sale is booked only under the `mccluster_org_id` it named. Without one it is skipped, never counted as house revenue. `checkout` now copies sale metadata onto the payment intent or subscription, so refunds and renewals can find the org.
- **Test mode.** Every row carries `livemode`. `/v1/work/history` excludes test money from billed, paid and verified totals and reports it as `test_mode_cents`; Control labels it "test mode, not revenue".
- **Control cannot retype provider facts.** On a provider-verified payment, amount, currency, provider, reference, state and paid_at are locked. On a Stripe order, amount, lines and placed_at are locked, but it still moves through fulfillment states. Resending a row unchanged is not an edit: instants are compared as instants and JSON is compared by content. The payment state cell is read-only for verified rows.

## Production

- `20261006021431_commerce_stripe_reconciler_v1` is applied. Before applying, the migration and the full SQL regression were dry-run against production in a forced-rollback transaction (`DRYRUN_OK`), and the rollback was verified clean.
- The repo file matches the stored production statement byte for byte (md5 `f59c1710…`).
- Production ledger and drift contract are at 269; `control-plane-drift-contract-check` is OK.
- All five functions are `security definer` with `search_path=""`; anon and authenticated cannot execute them, service_role can (verified live).

## Tests

- `supabase/tests/commerce_stripe_reconciler_regression.sql`: 10 sections, added to API Economic Core CI against a fresh rebuild.
- `scripts/test/stripe-commerce-reconciler.test.mjs`: event mapping, routing, signature-first ordering and the database boundary (6/6).
- `workers/mccluster/test/work-provider-verified.test.mjs`: locks and test-mode totals (5/5).
- Local runs: Worker suite 495/495, scripts suite 428/428, Core 271/271, EU source validator 1211/1211. Deno type-check passes for `stripe-webhook` and `checkout`.

## Not in this PR (staged, documented)

- **Square.** There is no Square webhook. Square payment links (the donation offering) and Square recurring plans are not reconciled.
- Client-facing deliverable approval, entitlement linkage and lead→relationship→project automation are the next #14 slices.

## Owner actions (`docs/control-plane/COMMERCE-RECONCILER.md`)

1. In the Stripe dashboard, confirm a webhook endpoint for `…/functions/v1/stripe-webhook` subscribed to `checkout.session.completed`, `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`, `checkout.session.expired`, `payment_intent.payment_failed`, `charge.refunded`, `invoice.paid`, `customer.subscription.deleted` and `account.updated`, plus a Connect endpoint for connected sellers.
2. Add the `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` Actions secret so the function deploy after merge is proven live.

## McCluster continuity

This implements browser-independent resident AI continuity and a persistent OVH workspace.

### Conversation durability
- reload newest 500 messages, not oldest 200
- reconcile unfinished durable compute tasks on reopen
- recover user turns saved before a compute task link was attached
- make ai.chat submission idempotent per durable user message
- mirror resident chat into private ai_context without creating objective-synthesis spam
- retrieve bounded relevant prior messages/memories before inference

### Persistent McCluster home
- adds bounded persistent VPS workspace under MCCLUSTER_HOME_ROOT
- standard directories: notes, artifacts, scratch, state, inbox, outbox
- list/read/write/status capabilities
- traversal and symlink escapes rejected
- bounded atomic writes
- included in core.resume
- exposed only through the reviewed owner MCP allowlist

Conversation truth remains in Supabase. Disposable code worktrees remain disposable.
